sights.w: A historic 2.5-acre estate garden in downtown Palo Alto, with formal rose and perennial beds, a wisteria arbor and the 1902 Gamble family house. A quiet horticultural retreat open daily during daylight hours.
sights.k: Grounds free and open every day at daylight; the Main House and offices keep weekday hours (roughly 9am-2pm). Donations encouraged.

sights.address: 3300 Page Mill Rd, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022
sights.w: A 1,400-acre Palo Alto nature preserve in the Santa Cruz Mountain foothills, with oak woodland trails, Boronda Lake and sweeping ridge views. Famous for being residents-only from 1969 until it finally opened to everyone in December 2020.
sights.k: Now open to all; a small per-vehicle entry fee applies and the lot can fill on weekends. Open sunrise to sunset.

sights.address: 51 S San Antonio Rd, Los Altos, CA 94022
sights.w: A free community museum telling the story of the Santa Clara Valley's orchard era and its turn into Silicon Valley, set on a campus beside the 1905 J. Gilbert Smith farmhouse. A gentle stop in downtown Los Altos.
sights.k: Free admission; open Thursday-Sunday, roughly noon-4pm. Closed major holidays.

sights.w: A beloved 32-acre Mountain View neighborhood park shaded by mature redwoods and oaks, with tennis courts, playgrounds, picnic lawns and a demonstration garden. A classic local weekend spot.
sights.k: Free; parking off Cuesta Dr fills on sunny weekends. Better as a picnic/family stop than a destination sight.

sights.w: The character-filled heart of downtown Sunnyvale: a block of restored late-1800s brick storefronts named for pioneer Martin Murphy Jr., now a pedestrian-only strip of restaurants, cafes and shops. Converted to a walking mall in 2023.
sights.k: Free to stroll; liveliest at the Saturday farmers market and in the evenings. On-street/garage parking nearby.

sights.w: A 177-acre bayfront park on the edge of the salt marsh, with seasonal wetlands, a large playground, picnic areas and flat trails linking to the Bay Trail. A joint city-county park good for birding and kite-flying.
sights.k: Per-vehicle parking fee on weekends and holidays; open 8am to 30 minutes after sunset. Windy near the marsh.

sights.w: A small volunteer-run museum housed in a replica of the historic Murphy family's Bay View farmhouse, set in Orchard Heritage Park amid one of the valley's last surviving apricot orchards. Free local history exhibits.
sights.k: Free; open limited hours (typically Tue/Thu/Sun afternoons). Combine with a walk through the adjacent heritage orchard.

sights.w: A green Sunnyvale neighborhood park with a pond, big playground, tennis and a walking loop shaded by palms and redwoods. An easygoing family stop away from the tech campuses.
sights.k: Free; mainly a picnic/playground park rather than a marquee sight.

sights.w: The walkable historic core of Saratoga along Big Basin Way (once 1850s 'Lumber Street'), lined with wine-country-style restaurants, galleries, boutiques and Blaney Plaza. The gateway to Hakone Gardens and Montalvo.
sights.k: Free to wander; parking on Big Basin Way and side lots. Best paired with a nearby garden or winery visit.

sights.w: A rustic 18-acre former horse ranch preserved as a nature area on Stevens Creek, with 1930s barns, a blacksmith shop, community gardens, a rotary nature museum and an environmental education center. A designated Cupertino natural preserve.
sights.k: Free; open daily 6am to dusk. Saturday open-house and last-Saturday blacksmith demos are the liveliest times.

sights.w: A free art museum on El Camino Real focused on Bay Area and California artists, with rotating exhibitions, a permanent collection and a sculpture garden on the grounds. A well-kept Santa Clara secret.
sights.k: Free admission and free parking; open Tuesday-Sunday, 11am-5pm, closed Mondays.

sights.address: 500 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95053
sights.w: Santa Clara University's free art and history museum, holding a California/mission-era collection and rotating fine-art shows, next to the historic Mission Santa Clara on the leafy campus. Accredited and free to all.
sights.k: Free; open Tuesday-Sunday afternoons, closed Mondays. Check the site as campus schedules shift hours.

sights.w: A 4,163-acre park on the grounds of the New Almaden mercury ('quicksilver') mines, which ran for 135 years and helped fuel the Gold Rush. Over 37 miles of trails wind past mine ruins, brick chimneys and hillside views above south San Jose.
sights.k: Free entry; hot and exposed in summer with little water. The nearby Casa Grande / New Almaden Quicksilver Mining Museum tells the mine story.

sights.w: A neoclassical Beaux-Arts temple built by the SFPUC in 1934 to mark where Hetch Hetchy water — piped 160 miles from Yosemite — arrives on the Peninsula, framed by cypress and a long reflecting pool. A striking, little-known monument near Woodside.
sights.k: Free; grounds open weekdays 9am-5pm, and to pedestrians/cyclists on weekends (the parking lot is closed weekends and holidays). Off Cañada Rd near I-280.

sights.address: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
sights.w: A pretty Santa Cruz cove named for its remaining natural rock arch, with tide pools and, from mid-October to mid-February, California's only State Monarch Butterfly Preserve, where thousands of monarchs cluster in the eucalyptus grove.
sights.k: Open 8am to sunset; parking about $10. Monarchs are seasonal (roughly November-January is peak) — the beach is worth it year-round.

sights.address: 701 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
sights.w: A scenic ~3-mile clifftop walking and biking path running from the wharf to Natural Bridges, overlooking Monterey Bay and the world-famous Steamer Lane surf break. Lighthouse Point holds the tiny Santa Cruz Surfing Museum.
sights.k: Free and always open; storm damage has closed short stretches to cars in recent years, but the coastal path remains the draw. Parking along the bluff.

sights.address: 465 Mystery Spot Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95065
sights.w: A classic 1940s roadside gravity-illusion attraction in the redwoods above Santa Cruz, where a tilted cabin makes balls appear to roll uphill and people seem to change height. A campy, only-in-California guided tour.
sights.k: Paid timed tours every half hour (~$12), plus $5 cash parking; it sells out midday. Arrive 30 minutes early. Open daily.

sights.w: A coastal state park just north of Santa Cruz combining a preserved 1800s dairy ranch (Victorian farmhouse, adobe, working blacksmith) with bluff-top trails over pocket beaches and tide pools. Popular with hikers and mountain bikers.
sights.k: Day-use parking about $10 (free on foot or bike); park open 8am-sunset, the historic Interpretive Center Thursday-Sunday.

sights.w: A 19th-century-style logging camp in Felton running two heritage trains: an 1890s narrow-gauge steam train that climbs through old-growth redwoods to Bear Mountain, and a diesel line down the San Lorenzo gorge to the Santa Cruz Boardwalk.
sights.k: Paid excursions; gates open 9am-5pm on operating days. Book steam-train tickets ahead, especially for holiday and Thomas events.

sights.w: One of the tallest lighthouses in the U.S. — a 115-foot 1872 tower on a dramatic bluff on the San Mateo coast, 5 miles south of Pescadero. A photogenic Highway 1 landmark now run as a state historic park (and hostel).
sights.k: Grounds free and open daily for photos and whale-watching; the tower itself has long been closed for restoration, so views are from the base. Bring a windbreaker.

sights.address: Mount Umunhum Rd, Los Gatos, CA 95033
sights.w: A 3,486-foot Santa Cruz Mountains peak inside Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve, crowned by 'the Cube' — the concrete base of a Cold War radar tower from the former Almaden Air Force Station. Reopened to the public in 2017 with 360-degree Bay-to-ocean views.
sights.k: Free; reach the summit by the paved Mount Umunhum Rd or a strenuous ~3.7-mile trail from the Bald Mountain lot. The narrow mountain road can close in bad weather — check before going.

sights.address: 1 Johnson Pier, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
sights.w: A working fishing harbor at Princeton-by-the-Sea and the launch point for Mavericks, the legendary big-wave surf break a half-mile offshore where winter swells top 60 feet. Harbor tide pools, seafood shacks and coastal trails round out a day.
sights.k: Harbor free to visit; to glimpse Mavericks, park at the Pillar Point bluff lot and walk the dirt trail. Big-wave season is roughly November-March.

sights.w: California's newest national park (2013): the eroded remnants of an ancient volcano, with jagged rock spires, talus caves and one of the best places in the state to spot free-flying California condors. A striking, harder-to-reach day trip southeast of Gilroy.
sights.k: About 1.5-2 hours from San Jose; the east and west entrances are NOT connected by road. Entry fee per vehicle; brutally hot in summer, best in spring. High Peaks Trail is the top condor spot.
